claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 has inherent or unacceptable residual porosity.
Residual porosity in conventional ZrB2 promotes hole formation and eventual failure during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Adding a small, controlled fraction of Ta to ZrB2 forms a (Zr,Ta)B2-based ceramic.
A liquid-precursor route can be used to prepare a Ta-containing diboride material with heat treatment near 1800 °C.
The modified ZrB2-Ta precursor should be sintered under an inert or reducing atmosphere.
Ta addition enables reactive liquid-phase sintering of ZrB2 at approximately 1800 °C.
A transient Ta-rich eutectic liquid phase forms during sintering.
The transient liquid phase enhances mass transport and promotes uniform densification.
Ta lowers the energy barrier for liquid-phase formation during sintering.
Enhanced low-temperature densification minimizes pore formation and residual porosity.
Reduced residual porosity improves structural integrity during exposure to aggressive liquid plating baths.
Ta-doped (Zr,Ta)B2 will achieve full densification at roughly 1800 °C.
Ta-doped (Zr,Ta)B2 will have significantly lower porosity and fewer microstructural defects than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Ta-doped (Zr,Ta)B2 will resist damage from prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure better than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
The anticipated processing benefit applies over an approximately 1800–2300 °C sintering range.
The proposed service boundary is exposure to liquid plating baths below the ceramic's stability limit.
The optimal Ta concentration and exact sintering conditions are not yet quantified.
